column3: The agroecological zone R1 covers mostly the southern districts of Maputo province including Matutuíne, Boane, Namaacha, Matola City, Moamba and Manhiça, Maputo City and southern Bilene district in Gaza province.
column4: The agroecological zone R1 is characterized mostly by rainfed agriculture, where during the rain seasons crops such as Maize, Groundnuts, Cassava and Sweet potatoes, and potatoes are practice. There are some irrigation activities for crops such as maize, beans, and horticulture that take place along the Maputo valley and Incomati, Umbeluzi and Limpopo rivers.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R2 extends from the eastern districts of Matutuíne, Manhiça and Marracuene in Maputo province, districts of Bilene, Xai-Xai, Chingoane and Mandlakazi in Gaza province and the province of Inhambane.
column4: Rainfed agriculture characterizes a major section of the coastal region south of Save, where the main crops during the rainy season include maize, cowpea groundnuts, sweet potato and cassava. Covering part of the Limpopo River in the south-east of Gaza province and south of Save in northern Inhambane, there are irrigation activities along these vales, mostly for rice crop, horticulture and fruit trees such as coconuts. Cashew nuts are also observed in this region.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R3 mostly covers the northern part of Moamba and Manhiça districts in Maputo province, western Inhambane province (Mabote district) and a major section of Gaza province.
column4: Although this region is characterized mostly by rainfed agriculture, there are fewer cropping activities as the region is less populated. However, some crops (including Sorghum) are grown in the region. Also, along the Limpopo River valley, irrigation activities are observed mostly for rice and horticulture.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R4 covers the district of Machazi to the southern part of the district of Guro in Manica province and districts of Gorongosa, Nhamatanda, and Chibabava in Sofala province.
column4: Covering high hills and plain sections of Manica and Sofala provinces, the R4 region is characterized by both rainfed and irrigated agriculture. Along with Manica province (mostly in the Sussundenga and Vanduzi districts), large farms equipped with irrigation tools are observed where crops such as soybean and maize are cultivated. In addition, fruit trees such as citrus, mango and banana are also farmed. Small farmers in both Manica and Sofala provinces do farm crops such as maize, sorghum and horticultural crops.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R5 covers part of Machaze district in Manica province, the coastal districts of Beira, Machanga, Chibabava, Buzi, Marromeu, Dondo, Muanza, and Cheringoma in Sofala province and the coastal districts of Luabo, Chinde, Mopeia, Inhassunge, Quelimane, Nicoadala, Maganja da costa, Mecubela and Mocuba in Zambézia province.
column4: Covering parts of the Buzi, Zambezi, Púnguè and Licungo basins, this region is characterized by both rainfed and irrigation agriculture. Rice is the predominant crop along with the heavy soils of Buzi, Machanga, Maganja da costa, and Nicoadala. In districts such as Dondo and Marromeu, large farmers (mostly sugar companies) practice, under irrigation sugar cane. Other crops in this region include chick-pea, pineapple, and sweet potatoes. Additionally, Cotton is grown as cash crop.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The coverage area of agroecological zone R6 includes the districts of Zumbo, Mágoe, Cahora-Bassa, Chiúta, Marara, Tete city, Moatize, Changara, Doa and Mutarara in Tete province, districts of Guro and Tambara in Manica province, Maringue, Chemba, Caia, Cheringoma, and Marromeu districts in Sofala province and western Mopeia and Morrumbala in Zambézia province.
column4: Located mostly over dryland areas of Tete, Manica and Sofala, the agriculture in the R6 region is mostly rainfed. Less/non-irrigation infrastructures are found and the region mostly cultivates tobacco as cash crop.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R7 covers the interior of Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Zambézia provinces, the Niassa province (excluding Lichinga district) and the districts of Moatize, Chiuta, Marávia, Macanga, Chifunde and Zumbo in Tete province.
column4: The agriculture in the R7 region is generally rainfed and the main crops include maize, sorghum, millet, cowpea, sesame and groundnuts. Cash crops such as cotton and tabaco are also produced.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R8 covers the coastal districts of Zambezia (Mulevala, Pebane, and Gilé), Nampula (Mogovolas, Moma, Larde, Angoche, Meconta, Liupo, Mogicual, Mussoril, Monapo, Nacala a velha and Memba) and Cabo Delgado (Mecufe, Pemba City, Ancuabe, Quissanga, Macomia, Muedumbe, Mocímbua da Praia, Nangade and Palma) provinces.
column4: Located along the coastal areas of Zambezia, Nampula and Cabo Delgado provinces, in the AEZ R8, rice is mostly produced along the heavy soils near the river banks. In this region, cashew nut is the most important cash crop. Fruit trees such as coconuts are cultivated along the districts of Zambezia province all year long.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R09 covers the north eastern part of Mueda district in Cabo Delgado province.
column4: The region is characterized by rainfed agriculture with maize as the main crop. In the R9 region, less/non-irrigation activity is developed.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)

column3: The agroecological zone R10 covers the districts of Marávia, Zumbo, Chifunde, Macanga, Angónia ,and Tsangano in Tete province, districts of Mulumbo, Namaroi, Alto Molócue, and Gùrué in Zambézia province, Malema in Nampula province and districts of Lichinga, Chimbunila, and Ngauma in Niassa province.
column4: Covering the high hills of Niassa, Tete and Zambezia provinces, this region is mostly characterized by rainfed agriculture with satisfactory rainfall and temperature all-year-long. Over the region, maize is the main crop practiced. Other crops over this region include soybean, cotton, tea, potatoes, groundnuts, and wheat.
column5: FAO Crop Calendar (Moçambique, zonas agroecológicas do IIAM)
